text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Military chiefs discuss latest bomb explosion, that rocked western Nigerian city of Ibadan on Monday, after a similar blast in Lagos last week; sources say army high command is embarrassed by the incidents.
- Government gives banks one week ultimatum to refund foreign exchange acquired from the weekly auction of foreign currency in contravention of rules governing the autonomous foreign exchange market.
- Youths attack on Shell oil company installations in the southeast causes a loss of 480,000 barrels of crude oil production in four days.
- Manufacturers association of Nigeria calls for prohibitive duties on imported goods to save the nation's industry from collapse.

- Government says it has no plans to devalue the naira currency any further and that its rising external reserves, now $6 billion compared with $4 billion last December will boost the value of the local currency.

- Delta state government sets up a three-man judicial commission to probe the conflict in the oil-producing town of Warri which led to the killing of scores of people and the disruption of crude oil production in the area.
- Shareholders of the Nigerian liquefied natural gas project endorse plan to expand its capacity by 200 percent by the year 2010.
- Nigeria may allot three oil fields to China for exploitation following recent visit to Abuja by Chinese prime minister Li Peng.
- Magistrate declines to strike out treason charge against exiled Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka and 11 other dissidents.
- An Air Guinea plane flying from Lagos to Conakry on Tuesday made an emergency landing at Lagos airport a few minutes after take-off following an outbreak of fire on board.
